input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: § 12.4 (duplicate-numbered) binds Customer with an undefined-scope, all-territory non-compete extending 24 months post-term, which exceeds the walk-away threshold on both scope and duration and contradicts the freedom-of-action acknowledgement Vendor gives in § 12.3. Preferred position is no non-compete on Customer, so we delete the clause and rely on § 12.3; the narrowed fallback (single named product, term only, 12 months, carve-outs) is offered in the comment.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept restrictions on the products or businesses we may build, buy, or sell, so we have deleted the 24-month, all-territory non-compete in 12.4, which also directly contradicts the freedom-of-action acknowledgement in 12.3. If you need protection for a specific offering, we could consider a term-only restriction on a single named competing product, capped at 12 months, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.summary: Delete the non-compete imposed on Customer in § 12.4.
